payload.name: ExtractExplicitUserStateDisclosures
payload.description: During extraction, when a user explicitly describes a current personal condition or stressor (e.g., dealing with work stress, feeling anxious), create a state memory candidate.
content: During candidate extraction, treat explicit first-person disclosures about the user's current state (e.g., 'dealing with work stress', 'feeling burned out') as `state` candidates even when they appear in casual or brief replies.
Record the condition, any stated cause or qualifier (e.g., work-related, family, health), the affected person, and resolve the time from the message/session timestamp.
Do not skip a disclosure just because it is an aside or the sentence also contains small talk; if the tracked user asserts an ongoing situation, it is memory-worthy evidence.

solves: The pipeline missed an explicit first-person disclosure of a user's current stressor because no candidate was extracted from a brief, casual conversational turn. Future sessions need a rule that explicit self-reports of ongoing personal states, including the cause or stressor, are memory-worthy state facts regardless of conversational framing. This applies whenever a tracked user states a current condition in their own words.
